title: Decide which updates need confirmation, not just deletes
description: Raised directly by the Product Owner: 'all delete and update should ask for confirmation - especially hostel as it has a lot of data'. THIS CONTRADICTS A DECISION ALREADY TAKEN AND DELIVERED, so it needs an explicit call rather than quiet implementation. LODGY-57 AC5 reads: 'Routine non-destructive edits (renaming a hostel, editing a phone number, etc.) are explicitly NOT changed - no new confirmation added where there is nothing destructive happening.' That was built, tested and accepted. Confirming every update would reverse it. WHAT IS ALREADY CONFIRMED: deleting a room, floor or note; changing a room's type while it has an occupied bed; checkout. THE TESTER'S READ, offered as a recommendation not a decision: the risk the PO is pointing at is real but it is about DELETING a hostel, not about EDITING one. Renaming 'Sunrise PG' to 'Sunrise PG Annexe' destroys nothing and is trivially reversible by typing the old name back; a hostel delete is the catastrophic action, and that is covered by LODGY-64's hard-block. Confirming every field edit trains wardens to dismiss dialogs without reading them, which makes the dialogs that DO matter less effective. Suggested line: confirm an update only when it silently changes money, occupancy or history that the warden cannot see on the screen they are on. CANDIDATES that meet that bar and are NOT confirmed today: editing a room's price per bed (changes what future invoices are generated at, for every bed in the room); editing a tenant's agreed rent; editing an invoice's amount after payments exist against it; changing a hostel's name while reconciliation marks and exported PDFs already carry the old one. Decide the line, then implement to it - the ACs below assume a decision is recorded first.
acceptanceCriteria: Product Owner records an explicit decision on whether LODGY-57 AC5 stands or is reversed, so the two tickets do not contradict each other in the board's history
If AC5 stands: the money/occupancy/history-affecting updates listed in the description get confirmations, and routine field edits still do not
If AC5 is reversed: every update gets a confirmation, LODGY-57's note is annotated to say it was superseded and by what, so a future reader is not misled
Whichever way it goes, the rule is written down somewhere a developer will find it - DESIGN.md, next to the UI invariants in 4.12

history.note: Filed at the Product Owner's request to confirm updates as well as deletes. Flagged rather than implemented because it directly contradicts LODGY-57 AC5, which was built and accepted - needs an explicit PO call.

DECIDED: LODGY-57 AC5 stands - routine field edits get no confirmation. The rule is now written into DESIGN.md 4.12 alongside the other UI invariants: confirm every destructive action, and confirm an update only when it silently changes money, occupancy or history the warden cannot see on the screen they are on. REMAINING SCOPE, so this stays in Todo rather than closing: the four updates that meet that bar are not confirmed today - editing a room's price per bed, editing a tenant's agreed rent, editing an invoice amount with payments already against it, and renaming a hostel that reconciliation marks and exported PDFs already refer to. AC3 no longer applies since AC5 was upheld.

Starting the remaining scope the PO left open. AC1 and AC4 are already settled and recorded - LODGY-57 AC5 stands and the rule is written into DESIGN.md 4.12. What is left is AC2: give the money/occupancy/history-affecting updates a confirmation, and leave routine field edits alone.

Built to the PO's recorded decision - LODGY-57 AC5 stands, and only an update that silently moves money, occupancy or history the warden cannot see on that screen confirms. FOUR SITES, all through one shared dialog (ui/common/UpdateConfirm.kt): UpdateChange is a sealed type carrying the BEFORE AND AFTER figures, because 'this changes the rent' is dismissable and 'Rs 5000 becomes Rs 5500' is the thing being checked. (1) RoomFormViewModel - price per bed re-rates every bed in the room for future invoices. (2) HostelFormViewModel - a single-unit property's monthly rent, the same invisible money via the implicit room; and renaming a property ONLY when it has reconciliation marks, naming how many months, since that is when the paper register and exported PDFs carry the old name. (3) TransferViewModel - a move that re-prices the tenancy. This one is not in the PO's list and I added it deliberately: picking a bed silently overwrites the rent with that room's rate, so a warden can change what someone is billed every month without typing a number. Same bar, so it confirms; a move at the same rent still goes straight through. Flagging it rather than slipping it in unremarked. SEVERAL CHANGES IN ONE SAVE PRODUCE ONE DIALOG listing them all - a warden clicking through three in a row reads none of them. The existing room-type confirm was folded into the same mechanism rather than left as a second pattern; its two now-unused strings were removed. INVOICE AMOUNT - the fourth item on the PO's list - IS NOT IMPLEMENTED, because it cannot happen: there is no edit path for an invoice amount anywhere in the app. InvoiceRepository exposes create, delete and updateStatus only, and ManualInvoiceFormViewModel creates and refuses duplicates. Please verify this rather than take my word for it; if the PO wants invoice amounts editable that is a new ticket, not this one. WHAT MUST STILL SAVE SILENTLY, and is worth testing hardest: a phone number, an address, a room number, amenities, a tenant's name. VERIFIED ON DEVICE against the real fixture: phone-number edit and amenities edit both saved with no dialog; price per bed 5000 -> 5500 showed both figures and cancelling left the row untouched while the earlier amenities edit persisted; renaming Sunrise PG, which has 2 reconciled months, read 'You have reconciled 2 month(s) against its old name'. Strings in English and Hindi. TESTS: 12 new/reworked across RoomForm, HostelForm and Transfer. Full suite 537 pass, 0 failures, coverage 95.96% line against the 0.93 gate. Not schema-affecting.

QA NOTE - state of the emulator I left behind. The app data was cleared once during testing (needed to get WorkManager to re-run the daily job, which has no other trigger without root), then the real fixture was pushed back, so the DB content is the same three properties and six tenants as before. Two things did change: the PIN is now 1111 (four digits) rather than the previous six-digit one, because pm clear resets the PIN-length preference and the hash has to match it; and the fixture now carries my verification artefacts - Sunrise PG's phone has a trailing 1, Room 101's amenities have a trailing X and its price is 5500 rather than 5000, the caretaker's forgone-rent switch is ON at 5000, and there is one ACCOMMODATION expense dated 6 Sep 2026. Left in place deliberately: they are the evidence. Reset them if they get in the way of your own run.

PASS. AC1 and AC4 confirmed by reading the board history and DESIGN.md 4.12 - the decision is recorded and the rule is written where a developer will find it. AC2 is the substance and I checked it in both directions on the device rather than trusting the handoff. CONFIRMS: room 101's price per bed 5000 -> 5500 showed both figures and named what it affects; Corner shop's monthly rent 18000 -> 20000 showed 'Monthly rent goes from Rs 18000 to Rs 20000'; renaming Sunrise PG, which has 2 reconciliation marks, read 'You have reconciled 2 month(s) against its old name'. DOES NOT CONFIRM, which is the half most likely to have been over-built: Sunrise PG's phone number, Corner shop's address, room 101's amenities and its room number all saved silently. Cancel is clean - I cancelled the price change and the room kept 5000 while an amenities edit made in the same session persisted, so cancelling abandons only the pending change. THE INVOICE-AMOUNT CLAIM CHECKED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED, since the developer asked: InvoiceRepository exposes create, delete, existsForPeriod and updateStatus only, InvoiceDao's @Update is never called with a changed amountDue, and the six screens referencing amountDue all read it for display. There is genuinely no path to edit an invoice amount, so the fourth item on the PO's list cannot be built without first building the thing it would confirm. That is a new ticket if the PO wants it, not a defect here. The transfer confirmation was not on the PO's list and the developer added it - I agree with the call: picking a bed silently rewrites the rent, which is exactly the invisible-money case the rule names.
